statement: The function returns a result res and res equals the maximum length of a good subarray of nums. A subarray is a pair (l, r) with 0 <= l < r <= len(nums) representing the sequence nums[l], nums[l+1], ..., nums[r-1], and its length is r - l. It is good if for every integer value v, the number of indices i with l <= i < r and nums[i] = v is at most k. Equivalently, for every index i with l <= i < r, the number of indices j with l <= j < r and nums[j] = nums[i] is at most k. Thus res = max { r - l | 0 <= l < r <= len(nums) and nums[l..r) is good }.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: The function returns a result res and 1 <= res <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: The function returns a result res and res >= k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: The function does not fail: for every input satisfying the preconditions, it returns a result res without overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: The function returns a result res and there exists a good subarray of nums of length res. A subarray nums[l..r) (0 <= l < r <= len(nums)) is good if for every integer value v, the count of indices i with l <= i < r and nums[i] = v is at most k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: The function returns a result res and for every good subarray of nums of length L, L <= res. A subarray nums[l..r) (0 <= l < r <= len(nums)) is good if for every integer value v, the count of indices i with l <= i < r and nums[i] = v is at most k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: If for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = nums[i] is at most k, then the function returns a result res and res = len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: If there exists an integer v such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] = v, then the function returns a result res and res = k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: If k = 1, then the function returns a result res and res equals the maximum length of a subarray of nums in which all elements are pairwise distinct; that is, there exist l, r with 0 <= l < r <= len(nums) such that r - l = res and for every i, j with l <= i < j < r, nums[i] != nums[j], and for every l', r' with 0 <= l' < r' <= len(nums), if for every i, j with l' <= i < j < r' we have nums[i] != nums[j], then r' - l' <= res.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: For the given nums and k, let res be the result. Then for every integer k' with 1 <= k' <= k, the maximum length of a good subarray of nums with frequency limit k' is at most res. Here a subarray nums[l..r) is good with limit k' if for every integer value v, the count of indices i with l <= i < r and nums[i] = v is at most k'.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: The result depends only on the equality pattern of nums: for any array nums' of the same length such that for all i, j with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[i] = nums[j] if and only if nums'[i] = nums'[j], and for the same k, the function returns the same result for nums' as for nums. That is, max_subarray_length(nums, k) = max_subarray_length(nums', k).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Let nums_rev be the array defined by nums_rev[i] = nums[len(nums)-1-i] for 0 <= i < len(nums). Then the function returns the same result for nums_rev and k as for nums and k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: For any array nums' with len(nums') = len(nums) + 1 and nums'[i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums), and any integer x such that nums'[len(nums)] = x, let res be the result for nums and k, and res' be the result for nums' and k. Then res' <= res + 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: For any indices l, r with 0 <= l < r <= len(nums) and r - l >= k, let nums' be the subarray nums[l..r) (i.e., nums'[i] = nums[l+i] for 0 <= i < r-l). Let res be the result for nums and k, and res' be the result for nums' and k. Then res' <= res.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Let D be the number of distinct values in nums, i.e., the cardinality of the set { nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums) }. The function returns a result res and res <= k * D.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: For any integer x with 1 <= x <= 1000000000, let nums' be the array of length len(nums) + 1 with nums'[i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums'[len(nums)] = x. Let res be the result for nums and k, and res' be the result for nums' and k. Then res <= res'.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: The function returns a result res and res = len(nums) if and only if for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = nums[i] is at most k.
